references.text: The description of the ark (הָאָרֹן) and the mercy seat (הַכַּפֹּרֶת) that Bezalel was to make, with detailed instructions for its construction.
Detailed instructions for the tabernacle (אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד) that Bezalel was commissioned to build.
Instructions for the altar and the courtyard, which are part of the equipment of the tabernacle (כְּלֵי הָאֹהֶל).
Moses calls craftsmen to make the tabernacle, the ark, the mercy seat, and all the equipment, parallel to what was commanded in 31:7.
The fulfillment of the command: Bezalel makes the ark (הָאָרֹן) and the mercy seat (הַכַּפֹּרֶת).
The raising of the tabernacle and the placement of the ark with the testimony and the mercy seat.
The mercy seat (הַכַּפֹּרֶת) over the ark of the testimony is mentioned as the place where God speaks to Moses.
The Letter to the Hebrews describes the ark of the covenant and the mercy seat (ἱλαστήριον) with the cherubim, pointing back to the tabernacle that Bezalel built.
Connects God's original command to the completion of all the equipment of the tabernacle.
Confirms that the most holy objects (the ark and the mercy seat) were made exactly as prescribed.
Complements 31:7 by showing that even the tent structure itself was built according to God's specific plan.
Describes the actual assembly and consecration of the objects that were commanded in 31:7.
Explains the theological function of the ark and the mercy seat mentioned in the source verse.
Clarifies what 'all the utensils of the tent' includes by listing the central altars and furnishings.
Places the mercy seat and the ark within the liturgical spatial arrangement before the altar of incense.
